title: Gardening & Plant Life

themePack.overview: Children investigate real plants and seeds through sensory soil play, planting, plant-part observation, and outdoor garden options when available. Balance nature science with process art and dramatic play (garden center, farmers market). Prioritize soil hygiene, seed safety for mixed ages, and respect for living things. Crafts support—not replace—real plant inquiry.
themePack.materials: Potting soil or kinetic sand alternative; pots; child watering cans; seeds appropriate for age (see safety); magnifying glasses; gardening gloves; artificial plants for dramatic play; fresh safe veggies for investigation (allergy-aware); paint/markers/paper; trays; handwashing station access; outdoor garden tools (child-sized) if outdoors; baskets for harvest play.
themePack.family: We are exploring seeds, soil, water, and sunlight—how plants grow. Ask your child what a seed needs. If you garden at home, invite them to water or notice leaves. Please share any seed/nut/plant allergies with us before tasting activities.
milestones: Language: Uses garden vocabulary—seed, soil, sprout, roots, stem, leaf, water, sunlight.
SEL: Shows care for living things; takes turns watering; cooperates in garden dramatic play.
Cognition: Sequences plant growth; compares plant parts; predicts what seeds need.
Motor: Scoops soil; pours water; fine motor seed sorting with safe sizes; garden yoga/movement.
Creativity: Process garden art and market play that reflect personal ideas, not identical crafts.

songs.title: Little Seed, Little Seed (LLH)
songs.lyrics:
Little seed, little seed, in the soil so snug,
Little seed, little seed, get a water hug.
Sunlight shines, roots grow down,
Stem reaches up above the ground.

Sprout, sprout, peeking through—
Growing green the whole week through!
songs.motions: Curl small as a seed; pat soil; rain fingers for water; arms up as stem; peek face on sprout.
songs.teacherDirections: Theme opener for Garden Sensory Bin and Planting Seeds Investigation. Use before outdoor watering when available.
songs.suggestedPace: Gentle; pause to “grow” slowly on the last lines.

songs.title: Roots, Stem, Leaves, and Flower (LLH Plant Parts)
songs.lyrics:
Roots go down to drink and hold,
Stem stands tall and brave and bold.
Leaves make food from air and light,
Flowers bloom—a colorful sight!

Roots, stem, leaves, flower—say it clear,
Plant parts help life grow each year.
songs.motions: Point down (roots); stand tall (stem); hands as leaves; circle arms as flower bloom.
songs.teacherDirections: Teach with a real plant or celery/lettuce sample during Plant Parts Investigation. Invite children to point on the plant as they sing.
songs.whenToUse: Science circle midweek; garden yoga warm-up.

songs.title: Watering Can Waltz (LLH)
songs.lyrics:
Tip the can, tip the can, water soft and slow,
Plants are thirsty—watch them grow.
Not too much and not too dry,
Garden helpers walking by.

Wash our hands when soil is done,
Gardening safely is garden fun!
songs.motions: Two-hand watering can tip; tiptoe “garden helper” walk; handwashing motions on last lines.
songs.teacherDirections: Use before Watering Relay and after soil play to cue hygiene. Outdoor option: sing while walking to garden beds.
songs.whenToUse: Before watering work; cleanup transition after soil bins.
songs.transitionPurpose: Ties care routines to hygiene and gentle watering.

songs.title: Harvest Helpers Hoedown (LLH)
songs.lyrics:
Pick, pick, harvest helpers go,
Basket full from head to toe!
Wash the veggies, market day—
Garden gifts we share and play.

Thank you soil, thank you sun,
Harvest helpers—everyone!
songs.motions: Picking motions; carry basket; scrub-wash hands/veggies; wave thank-you to sun.
songs.teacherDirections: Friday celebration and Farmer’s Market lead-in. If tasting, follow allergy protocols first.
songs.suggestedPace: Lively but controlled for indoor spaces.
songs.transitionPurpose: Celebrates care-to-harvest arc of the week.

books.title: From Seed to Plant
books.author: Gail Gibbons
books.why: Clear nonfiction plant science for preschool inquiry—supports planting and plant-parts talks.
before: What do you think a seed needs to grow?
during: What part is happening on this page—seed, sprout, or flower?
after: What will we give our classroom seeds this week?
How will we know if a seed is sprouting?
books.substitute: A Seed Is Sleepy by Dianna Hutts Aston

books.title: The Tiny Seed
books.author: Eric Carle
books.why: Story journey of a seed’s challenges and growth—builds empathy for living things and outdoor awareness.
before: What could happen to a tiny seed outdoors?
How can people help seeds grow?
during: What problem does the tiny seed face now?
How is the tiny seed different from the others?
after: What helped our tiny seed survive?
How will we be gentle with seeds and plants in class?
books.substitute: The Carrot Seed by Ruth Krauss

books.title: Planting a Rainbow
books.author: Lois Ehlert
books.why: Colorful seasonal planting and bloom cycle—pairs with flower garden painting and outdoor color hunts.
before: What colors have you seen in gardens?
What might we plant to make a rainbow garden?
during: Which flowers are bulbs? Which are seeds?
What colors are blooming now in the book?
after: Can we sort art scraps or flower pictures by color like a rainbow?
What outdoor colors can we find on a garden walk?

printableIdeas.title: Plant Life Cycle Sequencing Cards
printableIdeas.purpose: Large photo-style cards (seed → sprout → plant → flower) for Plant Life Cycle Craft discussion and sequencing—not a color-by-number worksheet.

printableIdeas.title: Seed Observation Mini Book
printableIdeas.purpose: Blank pages for Planting Seeds Investigation drawings/dictation across the week as sprouts change.

printableIdeas.title: Garden Center Price Tags / Market Labels
printableIdeas.purpose: Simple labels for Farmer’s Market and Garden Center Dramatic Play (soil, seeds, flowers, veggies).

themePack.safetyNotes: Soil hygiene: use clean potting soil; smocks; wash hands after every soil activity; no mouthing soil. Seed choking: for mixed ages or mouthing preschoolers, use large bean seeds only with strict supervision or substitute seed pictures/large counters; keep tiny seeds (like tomato) as teacher-handled demo only. Outdoor options: check for sharp sticks, insects, sun safety, and secure watering cans. Allergy: screen seed/nut/plant allergies before any tasting or flower handling; vegetable printing uses closed-skin veggies first. Tools are child-sized and plastic; adult controls any real trowels. Living plants: gentle hands; no pulling classmates’ sprouts.

notes: Do not use Dave Mallett Garden Song lyrics. Prefer LLH plant chants. Outdoor garden walk optional when space allows.
